messages:
Aisha: quick check — noticed a perf regression on the continuous-batcher after the kernel-fallback change. p95 jumped ~20ms on mid-length prompts (80-160 toks). Anyone else seeing this?
Ben: saw the alert in observability. It was correlated with increased KV-eviction churn. stack: batcher -> kernel-fallback -> decode path.
Kai: adding context: we changed kernel selection to prefer fallback when decode-rate estimator unstable. That reduces tail risk but fallback kernel is ~8% slower for 1-2 microbatched decodes.
Maya: here's a short repro profile I ran on a dedicated node: p50=14ms, p95=68ms before change; p50=15ms, p95=88ms after. throughput tokens/s down ~7%.
Ravi: important to confirm which cohorts are affected. My quick split by prompt length shows: short (<32) unaffected, mid (32-160) regressed, long (>160) slight improvement due to better KV priming.
Aisha: interesting — could KV priming be masking the long prompt gains? Maybe fallback kernel touches KV differently.
Ben: yes — fallback kernel currently does a smaller prefetch window which reduces early cache hits; for long prompts that reduces memory pressure and oddly improves steady decode rate. For mid prompts it increases roundtrips.
Kai: proposal: reclassify workload using a joint bucket on (prompt_len_bucket, decode_rate_bucket). We can keep current length buckets but split mid into mid-slow and mid-fast by decode rate.
Maya: agree. I ran a small experiment: mid-fast still suffers on fallback. mid-slow actually benefits because batching density improved.
Ravi: what about token budget targets? We default to token_budget=32 for mid. If we lower to 16 for mid-fast we might avoid fallback triggering.
Aisha: can we map this into the admission policy? e.g., if decode_rate > X and prompt_len in mid => prefer primary kernel and lower token_budget?
Kai: yes. Rough mapping I tested: decode_rate > 0.9 (tokens/ms) => force kernel_primary and token_budget=12; decode_rate < 0.4 => allow fallback and token_budget=48.
Ben: we should be careful: lowering token_budget increases microbatching overhead. For mid-fast it might help because it reduces queue waiting time, but for bursty tails it could increase overhead.
Maya: attached quick config snippet I used:
```
# admission config experiment
cohorts:
  mid-fast:
    length: [32, 160]
    decode_rate: [0.9, 999]
    token_budget: 12
    kernel_pref: primary
  mid-slow:
    length: [32, 160]
    decode_rate: [0, 0.9]
    token_budget: 48
    kernel_pref: fallback
```
Ravi: ran the above for 30m A/B on prod-canary: mid-fast p95 improved ~12ms, throughput +3%, overall p95 net -4ms. KV eviction rate dropped 18% for mid cohort.
Aisha: that's promising. Any observable regressions elsewhere?
SRE-bot: deploy-canary completed: canary-rsids 4/4 healthy, no new OOMs, disk IO stable.
Ben: one caveat — kernel selection change introduces a slight increase in CPU usage due to new decision logic (~3%). Preemptible infra saw occasional throttles.
Kai: we can micro-opt kernel decision (inline table mapping) to remove CPU overhead. Also consider moving rate-estimator to fast path cached per request for first 8 tokens.
Maya: also found a KV cache eviction pattern with token_budget >= 40: rapid fill and evict cycles on multi-tenant machines. Suggest adding per-tenant KV reservation or lowering budget for noisy tenants.
Ravi: proposal: add a soft limit per-tenant: token_budget_effective = min(global_budget, tenant_budget, 64) and evict if tenant_cache_size > tenant_limit. We can tune tenant_limit by p95 contribution.
Aisha: sounds good. Next steps?
Ben: 1) roll config to canary for 6 hours, monitor p95 and KV-evict-rate for mid cohorts. 2) add hotpath optimization for kernel selection. 3) add per-tenant KV soft limiter as follow-up.
Kai: I'll PR the admission rule change and the inline mapping.
Maya: I'll put the perf runs and traces in the batcher perf dashboard (links: https://perf.redwood/batcher/241987)
Ravi: I'll draft a short postmortem-ish note if this goes wider, so we track the root cause and mitigation.
Aisha: thanks all. If we see revert, do it fast. Also, annotate rollout with trace tags: cohort=mid-fast/mid-slow.
InfraBot: scheduled: canary rollout at 2026-03-18T19:00Z (trace tag: cohort-split). Monitoring alerts: p95-dropwatch, kv-evict-rate.
Ben: quick nit — add metric decode_kernel_latency.breakdown and kv.prefetch_hit_ratio to dashboard.
Kai: will do.
Maya: initial logs for the run: trace_id=trc_8f3a, sample stack: 
``
batcher: accept -> classify(mid-fast) -> kernel_primary -> decode -> emit
profiles: cpu 6%, gpu 72%, io 2%
```
Ravi: good capture. I'll keep the thread updated after 6h canary.
Aisha: perfect — thanks everyone :thumbsup:
